cards.power: Telekinetic Flop: Force an opponent to reroll a die. If they roll a 1, their weapon bends and breaks.
cards.lore: CIA verified he could see grapes in a box but failed to draw a bunny. Millions spent on parlor tricks.
cards.gradeReason: Uri Geller energy is clear, but 'reroll' mechanic doesn't quite embody bending reality.
cards.artworkPrompt: Retro spy dossier style. Fox in Hawaiian shirt bending a spoon. Mood: fraudulent confidence.

cards.power: Remote View: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Keep one, burn the rest.
cards.lore: 15% accuracy rate deemed "successful" by desperate bureaucrats terrified of Soviet mind-wizards.
cards.gradeReason: Remote View + burn the rest = instant psychic spy roleplay. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Classified document aesthetic. Owl with headphones and third eye. Mood: tense Cold War paranoia.

cards.power: Coordinate Lock: Guess a number. If the opponent rolls it, you steal their turn.
cards.lore: Recruited because he was annoying and persistent. Claimed to see Jupiter; mostly saw his own ego.
cards.gradeReason: Peacock painting GPS coordinates is vivid, but 'guess a number' mechanic needs explaining.
cards.artworkPrompt: Vintage spy recruitment poster. Peacock at easel with GPS coordinates. Mood: deluded self-importance.

cards.power: Drunken Insight: Gain +2 to rolls, but you must discard a card at random due to hangover.
cards.lore: Intelligence gathered so unbelievable, agents required eight martinis to process the report.
cards.gradeReason: The drunk bonus/hangover penalty is fun, but the psychic program context is background, not foreground.
cards.artworkPrompt: Intelligence file aesthetic. Military goat surrounded by empty martini glasses, maps. Mood: boozy incompetence.

cards.power: Chemical Chaos: Swap the stats of two target cards for one round.
cards.lore: The goal was to destroy the human ego. The result was lawsuits and bad trips.
cards.gradeReason: LSD dispenser + swap stats = you ARE MKUltra. Mechanic perfectly mirrors the chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: MKUltra dossier style. Vulture in lab coat pouring LSD into water cooler. Mood: unhinged scientific authority.

cards.power: Blackmail Tape: Opponent must show you their hand. You pick one card to discard.
cards.lore: CIA agents running a brothel to watch people on acid. "Fun, fun, fun," said the agent in charge.
cards.gradeReason: Blackmail Tape is pure spy power. Opponent shows hand, you discard one — total exposure, total control.
cards.artworkPrompt: Noir surveillance photograph style. Rat in trench coat watching guinea pigs through window. Mood: seedy bureaucratic voyeurism.

cards.power: Bad Serve: Inflict "Confusion" status. Opponent cannot use Action cards next turn.
cards.lore: Went in for depression, injected with fatal MDA overdose. The government covered it up for 20 years.
cards.gradeReason: Bad Serve/Confusion is mechanically clear but the Harold Blauer MKUltra reference needs knowing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tennis club vintage print. Dog in whites holding snake-racket, psychedelic background. Mood: drugged disorientation.

cards.power: Defenestration: Remove a character card from play permanently.
cards.lore: Spiked by his boss, then fell 13 floors. "Suicide," they said. We have the receipt.
cards.gradeReason: Defenestration removes a card permanently. Frank Olson energy is immediately embodied — no rules needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cold War document aesthetic. Blue bird in suit falling from window with TOP SECRET folder. Mood: grim institutional murder.

cards.power: Astral Projection: Ignore all damage this turn. You are not currently in this dimension.
cards.lore: CIA report confirms: Reality is a hologram, and you can escape it if you listen to this tape long enough.
cards.gradeReason: 'You are not currently in this dimension' — player knows exactly what to perform. Transcendent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Classified report cover aesthetic. Meditating sloth dissolving into binary hologram. Mood: bureaucratic mysticism.

cards.power: Memory Wipe: Shuffle the discard pile back into the deck. Everyone forgets what happened.
cards.lore: "Depatterning" meant erasing the mind to rebuild it. They only succeeded in the erasing part.
cards.gradeReason: Memory Wipe is mechanically clear; the Cameron MKUltra connection deepens it but isn't required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Reel-to-reel tape recorder blueprint. Crocodile doctor wiring up terrified rabbit. Mood: clinical horror with corporate cheerfulness.

cards.power: Earworm: Opponent must sing a song or lose 1 HP.
cards.lore: "I Love You" played at ear-splitting volume for 24 hours. Interrogation via nursery rhyme.
cards.gradeReason: Must sing or lose HP — instant table chaos. No context required. Everyone knows what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Guantanamo-adjacent dossier. Purple tyrannosaur raging with musical notes, tiny hamster cowering. Mood: absurd psychological warfare.

cards.power: Spill the Beans: Opponent must reveal their hidden objective card.
cards.lore: There is no truth serum. Just drugs that make you ramble about your mother until you pass out.
cards.gradeReason: Reveal hidden objective is clear, but the nihilist lore ('there is no truth serum') is the real hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Laboratory evidence photo. Coiled snake around rainbow syringe. Mood: pharmaceutical deception.

cards.power: Distracted Asset: Flip a coin. Heads: Spy on hand. Tails: Get hit by a taxi (Discard card).
cards.lore: $20 Million to put a microphone in a cat. Hit by a taxi on its first mission. Peak efficiency.
cards.gradeReason: Coin flip — spy or get hit by taxi. The CIA cat is immediately playable and tragic. Pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cold War technical schematic. Wired-up cat with circuit diagrams, microphone implant visible. Mood: expensive bureaucratic absurdity.

cards.power: Aerial Recon: Reveal the top card of the deck.
cards.lore: The only spy that works for breadcrumbs and craps on the target. Statistically more reliable than the CIA.
cards.gradeReason: Pigeon spy with camera = reveal top card. Immediately embodies the surveillance asset. Perfect alignment.
cards.artworkPrompt: WWII reconnaissance photo aesthetic. Pigeon strapped with giant camera lens, blueprints background. Mood: overlooked competence.

cards.power: Scent Failure: Your attacks miss this turn because the enemy smells like snacks.
cards.lore: MI6 thought aniseed was irresistible to tracker dogs. The dogs preferred the actual spy.
cards.gradeReason: Attacks miss because enemy smells like snacks — funny concept, but needs the MI6 context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: British intelligence file. Bloodhound detective distracted by giant steak, spy escaping background. Mood: delicious incompetence.

cards.power: Psychological Warfare: Opponent is 'Spooked' and drops one item card.
cards.lore: OSS painted foxes to look like spirits to scare enemies. The foxes just licked the paint off.
cards.gradeReason: 'Spooked' status is clear but depends on table knowing the Psychological Warfare category.
cards.artworkPrompt: OSS field manual illustration. Bioluminescent fox skeleton glowing in dark forest, confused woodland creatures. Mood: failed supernatural terror.

cards.power: Cold Case: Eliminate a target. No evidence remains. The kill is untraceable.
cards.lore: Fires a frozen dart of shellfish toxin. The dart melts. The victim dies. The perfect crime, brought to you by tax dollars.
cards.gradeReason: Eliminate target, no evidence, untraceable — every word embodies the weapon. Instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: CIA equipment inventory photo. Snake in tuxedo aiming frozen-dart pistol. Mood: tax-funded bureaucratic assassination.

cards.power: Kiss of Death: If engaged in close combat, automatic critical hit.
cards.lore: The "Kiss of Death." For when you need to touch up your lips and blow someone's brains out simultaneously.
cards.gradeReason: Kiss of Death + auto crit in close combat. Mechanic IS the weapon. Iconic, immediately performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: KGB beauty counter aesthetic. Glamorous poodle applying lipstick-pistol at vanity mirror. Mood: lethal femininity.

cards.power: Morning Breath: Target takes poison damage over 3 turns.
cards.lore: Designed for Patrice Lumumba. The agent in charge threw it in the Congo River instead. Even spies have limits.
cards.gradeReason: Morning Breath DoT is clear; Lumumba context adds weight but isn't required to play the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tropical operation dossier. Crocodile in bathroom brushing teeth with toxic green paste. Mood: reluctant assassin.

cards.power: Booby Trap: Place face down. If revealed, 5 damage to all players.
cards.lore: Painted to attract Castro while diving. Intended to blow his face off. Never planted.
cards.gradeReason: Face-down trap, 5 damage on reveal — you ARE the Acme scheme. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: ACME trap company diagram. Hermit crab in explosive seashell, clock mechanism visible. Mood: cartoon-level assassination attempt.

cards.power: Decoy: Negate one attack. The enemy hits the doll instead.
cards.lore: A CIA "Sex Doll" used to fool KGB tails in Moscow. It pops up in 4 seconds. Don't ask what else it does.
cards.gradeReason: Decoy/negate is mechanically sound, but the CIA sex doll lore does the heavy lifting here.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cold War surveillance photo. Bear driving car, sheep jack-in-the-box popping from briefcase. Mood: embarrassing tradecraft.

cards.power: Organic Chemistry: Write a secret order. It can only be revealed by "heating" (rolling a 6).
cards.lore: MI6 Chief Mansfield Cumming discovered it made great invisible ink. The smell, however, was a dead giveaway.
cards.gradeReason: Write a secret order only revealed on a 6 — hilariously embodied, instantly performative at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: MI6 laboratory report aesthetic. Badger in lab coat holding test tube with dubious expression. Mood: accidental discovery.

cards.power: Sugar Rush: Blow up a target asset. Replace it with a recipe for Red Velvet.
cards.lore: MI6 hacked an Al-Qaeda magazine and replaced bomb recipes with Ellen DeGeneres' cupcake instructions.
cards.gradeReason: Blow up asset, replace with cupcake recipe — the mechanic IS the operation. Instant iconic play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Baking show gone wrong aesthetic. Bear in chef hat mixing C4 explosive into cupcake batter. Mood: domestic subversion.

cards.power: Monsoon: All players are bogged down. Movement speed reduced to 0.
cards.lore: Operation Popeye. Weaponized rain to wash away the Ho Chi Minh trail. Now a war crime!
cards.gradeReason: Monsoon/movement to 0 is clear but a step removed from the weather manipulation concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Vietnam War aerial operation map. Frog in biplane flying through weaponized rainstorm over jungle. Mood: environmental warfare hubris.

cards.power: Humiliation: Target loses all 'Charisma' bonuses.
cards.lore: Thallium powder in his shoes. The goal wasn't to kill him, but to make his hair fall out and destroy his machismo.
cards.gradeReason: Lose Charisma is thematically perfect but depends on knowing Castro as the target.
cards.artworkPrompt: CIA assassination memo aesthetic. Military goat losing magnificent beard in a cloud of dust. Mood: political emasculation.

cards.power: Frozen Asset: Target is paralyzed for 2 turns.
cards.lore: The closest they ever got. The pill froze to the freezer lining and broke when the assassin tried to retrieve it.
cards.gradeReason: Frozen Asset/paralysis is mechanically clean; the milkshake Castro assassination attempt adds perfect flavor.
cards.artworkPrompt: 1960s diner receipt aesthetic. Cow waiter serving poison milkshake, skull-and-crossbones ice cream. Mood: botched glamour.

cards.power: Seduction Fail: You cannot attack the target. You fall in love instead.
cards.lore: She hid the poison pills in her cold cream. They dissolved. Castro handed her his gun. She couldn't shoot.
cards.gradeReason: 'You fall in love instead' — anti-power power move. Player knows exactly what to perform. Hilarious G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tropicana spy glamour aesthetic. Cat in red dress holding cold cream jar, gun on table untouched. Mood: weaponized romance failure.

cards.power: Broadcast Jam: Silence an opponent's Ability for one round.
cards.lore: Plan: Spray the broadcast booth with LSD so he rambles like a maniac on live air.
cards.gradeReason: Silence ability is clear; the LSD broadcast plan reference requires knowing the CIA Cuba psyops.
cards.artworkPrompt: Radio station on-air light aesthetic. Psychedelic parrot in military uniform screaming at microphone. Mood: chemically induced chaos.

cards.power: Superstition: Fear check. If failed, enemy unit flees the battlefield.
cards.lore: CIA drained the blood of Huk rebels in the Philippines to simulate "Aswang" vampire attacks. It worked.
cards.gradeReason: Fear check — enemy flees. You ARE the psychological warfare operation. Mechanic mirrors the terror.
cards.artworkPrompt: Philippine folklore meets CIA field report. Bat agent in sunglasses draining blood from rebel soldier. Mood: colonial supernatural horror.

cards.power: Bad OpSec: Reveal all players' hands.
cards.lore: US spies in Beirut used "PIZZA" as a code word. Hezbollah figured it out. They never ordered takeout again.
cards.gradeReason: Bad OpSec reveals ALL hands — pure chaos play, immediately funny, no context required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Beirut safe house aesthetic. Rat on moped delivering TOP SECRET pizza box, surveillance van background. Mood: catastrophic tradecraft.

cards.power: Strange Bedfellows: Gain control of a neutral NPC.
cards.lore: CIA bribed Afghan warlords with Viagra. "Reignited the sex life of a patriarch." Information flowed immediately.
cards.gradeReason: Strange Bedfellows gains neutral NPC — mechanic perfectly mirrors the bribery operation. Instant table gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: US Embassy dispatch aesthetic. Lion warlord holding Viagra bottle, grateful expression. Mood: pharmaceutical diplomacy.

cards.power: Consumer Flop: This card has no effect. It is just embarrassing.
cards.lore: "Devil Eyes." A toy designed to scare kids away from Al-Qaeda. Instead, it became a collector's item.
cards.gradeReason: 'This card has no effect. It is just embarrassing.' — meta-comedy perfection. Play it and own the failure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collector's item packaging aesthetic. Wolf creature in cheap 'Devil Eyes' blister pack. Mood: Pentagon procurement disaster.

cards.power: False Flag: Attack your own unit to gain +10 Attack against an enemy next turn.
cards.lore: The Joint Chiefs wanted to bomb Miami and blame Cuba. Kennedy said no.
cards.gradeReason: Attack your own unit for +10 — you ARE the false flag. Mechanic demands the betrayal be performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Top Secret war room diagram. Wolf in lamb's clothing staging model ship explosion in bathtub labeled MIAMI. Mood: military bureaucratic treachery.

cards.power: Puppet Master: Replace the current game leader with a player of your choice.
cards.lore: Operation Ajax. Overthrew a [REDACTED] because of oil. The bill came due in 1979.
cards.gradeReason: Replace game leader with your choice — pure power play. You're the CIA installing a puppet. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Oil barrel Cold War dossier. Gorilla in suit controlling Persian cat leader like a marionette. Mood: imperial resource management.

cards.power: Constitutional Crisis: End the current turn immediately.
cards.lore: The CIA hated the Australian PM. The Queen's rep fired him. "God Save the Queen," indeed.
cards.gradeReason: Constitutional Crisis end-turn is abstract — strong historical event, mechanic doesn't quite embody the drama.
cards.artworkPrompt: Royal Gazette announcement aesthetic. Corgi in crown handing dismissal letter to surprised kangaroo. Mood: constitutional absurdity.

cards.power: Psychological Break: Target player must discard their best card or lose the game.
cards.lore: "You are an evil beast." The FBI sent MLK a letter urging him to kill himself. Signed, "A Friend."
cards.gradeReason: Discard best card or lose — devastating psychological mechanic. You perform the FBI letter. Chilling G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: FBI typewriter carbon copy aesthetic. Hyena in suit typing MLK threat letter, reels of wire recording. Mood: institutional malevolence.

cards.power: Recover Tech: Draw 2 gadget cards.
cards.lore: A silent red ball crashed. Left behind gold wire and mesh nets. Someone came back to clean it up.
cards.gradeReason: Draw 2 gadget cards is purely mechanical — the Hill 611 UFO lore is the card's strength.
cards.artworkPrompt: Soviet field report aesthetic. Bear soldier examining red geodesic sphere in snow, gold wire visible. Mood: Cold War reverse engineering.

cards.power: Paralysis: Target player cannot move for one round.
cards.lore: Three-meter tall aliens with three eyes landed in a park. Kids drew them. Adults were too scared to talk.
cards.gradeReason: Cyrillic title + three-eyed giants in a Soviet park — paralysis mechanic is embodied by sheer spectacle.
cards.artworkPrompt: Soviet children's drawing aesthetic. Three-eyed robot alien in Voronezh park, children sketching, adults fleeing. Mood: provincial Soviet terror.

cards.power: Atmospheric Phenom: Change the environment card to "Red Rain."
cards.lore: Petrozavodsk incident. A giant jellyfish rained light on the city. Smashed windows. The Kremlin shrugged.
cards.gradeReason: Change environment to Red Rain is interesting but abstract — needs the Petrozavodsk jellyfish context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Soviet port incident report aesthetic. Giant luminescent jellyfish raining laser light on Petrozavodsk harbor. Mood: cosmic indifference.

cards.power: Launch Sequence: Roll a D6. On a 6, destroy all cards on the table.
cards.lore: A UFO hovered over a silo in Ukraine. The nukes activated themselves. World War III was 10 seconds away.
cards.gradeReason: Roll D6, on 6 all cards destroyed — nuclear stakes are immediate. Table goes silent when you play this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Soviet nuclear launch terminal aesthetic. Dog general watching UFO trigger warning alarm at silo console. Mood: existential accidental apocalypse.

cards.power: Cover Up: Turn a 'True' card into a 'Fake' card.
cards.lore: First they said it was a saucer. Then they said it was a weather balloon. The rancher said it was "sticks and tape."
cards.gradeReason: Turn True into Fake — this IS kayfabe. The ur-cover-up. Every player knows what they're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: 1947 news clipping aesthetic. Sheep farmer staring at crashed saucer, government vehicles approaching. Mood: American mythology in real time.

cards.power: Impossible Maneuver: Dodge any attack perfectly.
cards.lore: USS Nimitz. No wings. No exhaust. Dropped 80,000 feet in a second. "We don't know what it is."
cards.gradeReason: Dodge any attack perfectly. You ARE the UAP — no physics apply. Immediate and thrilling to play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Navy aviator radar screen aesthetic. Tic-tac UFO blip vanishing from penguin pilot's display. Mood: physics-defying nonchalance.

cards.power: High Strangeness: Spawn a random monster token.
cards.lore: Poltergeists, cattle mutilation, and invincible wolves. The DIA spent $22 million to study a haunted ranch.
cards.gradeReason: Random monster token is fun but mechanical — the $22M haunted ranch lore is where the performance lives.
cards.artworkPrompt: Paranormal investigation field report. Wolf and bull on haunted Utah ranch, hovering orbs, camera crew. Mood: expensive supernatural confusion.

cards.power: Siege: You cannot leave your current location. Defense +5.
cards.lore: Kelly-Hopkinsville. A family fought a gun battle with "silver goblins" all night. Police found bullet holes, but no bodies.
cards.gradeReason: Siege/Defense is clearly mechanical — the Kentucky silver goblin gun battle lore sells the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: 1955 police report aesthetic. Silver owl-alien at Kentucky farmhouse window, bullet holes in wall. Mood: rural American alien terror.

cards.power: Nuclear Target: This card draws all enemy fire.
cards.lore: Soviet satellites saw generals converging here daily. They thought it was a secret bunker. It was a lunch counter.
cards.gradeReason: Draw all enemy fire is mechanically clear; the Pentagon hot dog stand lore is funnier than the mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pentagon aerial satellite photograph aesthetic. Pig general eating hot dog in labyrinthine building courtyard. Mood: accidental disinformation.

cards.power: Leak: Reveal the entire deck to all players.
cards.lore: Top secret Pentagon war plans leaked on a Discord server. By a 21-year-old. To impress his teen friends.
cards.gradeReason: Reveal the ENTIRE deck — pure chaos. You're the Discord leaker. Mechanic is immediate and devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Discord server screenshot aesthetic. Young otter in headset streaming Pentagon documents on gaming setup. Mood: catastrophic social media oversharing.

cards.power: Redaction: Cancel a played "Lore" card.
cards.lore: They tried to pass a law to reveal the aliens. The Defense contractors said "No." Democracy in action.
cards.gradeReason: Cancel a Lore card is thematically perfect but needs the Schumer UAP disclosure context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Congressional hearing redacted transcript aesthetic. Frog senator feeding UFO disclosure papers into shredder. Mood: democratic obstruction.

cards.power: Speed Demon: Move anywhere on the board instantly.
cards.lore: Area 51 wasn't for aliens. It was for planes so fast they melted their own paint. Most UFOs were just us.
cards.gradeReason: Move anywhere instantly — you ARE the SR-71. Mechanic embodies the plane perfectly. Clean G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Area 51 test flight log aesthetic. SR-71 Blackbird piloted by gecko, paint melting at Mach 3. Mood: classified speed.

cards.power: Give Peace a Chance: Prevent all combat for one round.
cards.lore: Nixon wanted him deported. The FBI tracked him for years. Even noted his parrot, "Linda."
cards.gradeReason: Give Peace a Chance prevents all combat — you ARE John Lennon. Mechanic mirrors the political threat.
cards.artworkPrompt: FBI surveillance file aesthetic. Walrus with peace sign and parrot, surveillance team watching from van. Mood: paranoid pacifism.

cards.power: Scandal: Target player loses reputation.
cards.lore: Investigated for sleeping with communists (and Kennedys). The file is still redacted.
cards.gradeReason: Scandal/lose reputation is clear but the anonymous 'The Blonde' needs knowing to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Redacted FBI file aesthetic. Blonde bombshell poodle in white dress, dark surveillance figure in bushes. Mood: American mythology surveillance.

cards.power: Exile: Force a player to leave the room for 1 minute.
cards.lore: MI5 blocked his return to the US. "Premature Anti-Fascist." Too woke for 1952.
cards.gradeReason: Force player to leave room is a wild mechanic — but requires knowing Chaplin's story to embody it fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Passport denial stamp aesthetic. Penguin in bowler hat blocked by bulldog policeman with STOP sign. Mood: political exile absurdity.

cards.power: Mob Ties: Summon a 'Thug' token to fight for you.
cards.lore: 2,000 page FBI file. He offered to be a CIA courier. They declined.
cards.gradeReason: Mob Ties/Thug token is clear, but the Frank Sinatra FBI context is needed to perform the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Rat Pack Vegas aesthetic. Golden retriever in tuxedo shaking hands with mob otter, FBI tail visible. Mood: glamorous surveillance.

cards.power: Infiltrate: Look at opponent's hand. If they have a "Protest" card, discard it.
cards.lore: "Neutralize, disrupt, discredit." The FBI declared war on civil rights.
cards.gradeReason: Discard Protest card from hand — you ARE COINTELPRO. Mechanic embodies the operation precisely. Chilling.
cards.artworkPrompt: FBI infiltration file aesthetic. Chameleon in fedora embedded in ant civil rights march. Mood: institutional betrayal.

cards.power: Witch Hunt: Remove all "Fabulous" cards from the game.
cards.lore: Thousands fired for being gay. "Security risks," said Hoover (who wore tulle at private parties, allegedly).
cards.gradeReason: Remove all Fabulous cards — perfectly named, perfectly hypocritical. Player knows what to perform instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: State Department hearing aesthetic. Bulldog in suit firing pink flamingo employee, tulle peeking from briefcase. Mood: spectacular hypocrisy.

cards.power: Martyrdom: If this card is destroyed, all allies gain +5 Attack.
cards.lore: Drugged by an informant. Shot in his bed. He was 21.
cards.gradeReason: Allies gain +5 when destroyed — Fred Hampton's martyrdom embodied mechanically. Devastating and powerful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Black Panther chapter meeting aesthetic. Sleeping raccoon surrounded by shadowed figures, allies rallying outside. Mood: state-sanctioned tragedy.

cards.power: Turf War: Force two opponents to fight each other.
cards.lore: FBI tried to start a war between the Mob and the Communist Party. Neither side took the bait.
cards.gradeReason: Force two opponents to fight is clear — the FBI Mob/Communist chaos-sowing context deepens it.
cards.artworkPrompt: FBI strategy memo aesthetic. Weasel agent holding Mafia and Communist Party files, making both sides glare at each other. Mood: failed divide and conquer.

cards.power: Impossible Lock: Trap an opponent. They cannot escape until they roll a 6.
cards.lore: MI6 math genius found padlocked in a bag. "Accident," said the coroner. "Impossible," said the locksmith.
cards.gradeReason: Trap opponent until they roll a 6 — you perform the impossible murder mystery. Immediate and eerie.
cards.artworkPrompt: Scotland Yard evidence photograph. Hamster in North Face bag padlocked in bathtub. Mood: classified impossibility.

cards.power: Double Agent: You win the game if you are the only player with 0 cards left.
cards.lore: FBI agent spying for Russia for 22 years. He sold them the tunnel we dug under their embassy.
cards.gradeReason: Win with 0 cards — you've sold everything. Robert Hanssen's betrayal made a perfect alternative win-con.
cards.artworkPrompt: Soviet embassy tunnel blueprint aesthetic. Mole in FBI suit digging under embassy building. Mood: long-game institutional betrayal.

cards.power: Old Boys Club: You cannot be arrested or attacked by "Authority" cards.
cards.lore: Top MI6 agents working for the KGB. They were never caught because they were "gentlemen."
cards.gradeReason: Immune to Authority cards is perfect for Cambridge Five, but needs the class-privilege context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gentleman's club portrait aesthetic. Badgers and bear in tweed toasting with vodka, KGB medals under lapels. Mood: aristocratic treason.

cards.power: Bad Disguise: You are instantly detected. But you look fabulous.
cards.lore: MI6 master spy arrested in Madrid in drag. Claimed it was "for a joke." The Spanish police were unamused.
cards.gradeReason: 'You are instantly detected. But you look fabulous.' — anti-stealth power move. Pure comedy G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Spanish police booking photo aesthetic. Fox in flamboyant floral dress being escorted by two bull officers. Mood: fabulous operational failure.

verdict: Project Gateway Kayfabe operates at peak FrizzleBob altitude — sixty cards of CIA black ops, psychic warfare, vampire psy-ops, and cupcake bombs that hit with documentary precision. Named strength: lore-mechanic alignment is nearly flawless (Defenestration removes cards permanently; Double Agent wins on zero cards; The Demonic Toy does nothing and admits it). Named weakness: the four Russian-language Cyrillic cards are visually spectacular but create a translation hurdle at English-only tables. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: Sixty historically grounded cards where every CIA failure, cover-up, and black program becomes a playable power. For anyone who suspected the truth was stranger — and was right.

Page 10 is all-Russian Cyrillic (ХИЛЛ 611, ВОРОНЕЖСКИЕ ГИГАНТЫ, МЕДУЗА, ЯДЕРНЫЙ ПЕРЕОПРЕДЕЛИТЕЛЬ) — exceptional visual distinction, translation needed for English tables. marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PROJECT GATEWAY – The CIA's Real Black Budget, Dealt Face-Up (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The agency once wired a live cat for sound and walked it past a Soviet embassy. That program had a code name, a budget, and a final report.

Operation Midnight Climax was real: a safehouse, a two-way mirror, and citizens dosed with LSD while agents watched and took notes. It had an accountant. So did the remote-viewing unit, the heart-attack pistol, and a dozen schemes that read like a fever dream but came with a signature at the bottom. You do not have to invent a conspiracy here. The strange part of this archive is that the strangest pages are the documented ones, sitting in a folder with a line item, waiting for someone to read them out loud.

Project Gateway Kayfabe is declassified history you play with a straight face. Sixty cut-and-play cards take every failure, cover-up, and black program and hand it back to you as a move you run on purpose, in front of witnesses. It is Social Story Wrestling for the reading-room crowd: you perform the official record card by card, and the table decides what survives contact with everything everyone already suspects.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Project Gateway Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Operation Midnight Climax, The Demonic Toy, and The Cross-Dresser.
